mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% mean) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a simultaneous drop in housing starts (HOUST) below their 12-month moving average signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST < 12-month moving average for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% mean) during periods when both GDPC1 YoY < -2% and HOUST is below its 12-month moving average for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profit margins, which in turn drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% mean) during periods when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by >0.5% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.8% mean) during periods of three consecutive months of >0.5% monthly INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise of more than 3% in both real personal savings (RSAFS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within a single month signals a shift from consumption to precautionary saving, reducing aggregate demand and corporate sales, which results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous month +3% AND UNRATE > previous month +0.3pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5% mean) during months when both RSAFS and UNRATE rise by more than their respective thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises by more than 4% year-over-year while the federal funds rate remains below 2% for at least six months, it signals insufficient monetary tightening to contain inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL YoY > 4% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for at least 6 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.2% mean) during periods of >4% YoY CPI and FEDFUNDS < 2% for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 0.5 percentage points in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) for four consecutive months signals persistent labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.0% mean) during periods of four consecutive months of UNRATE rising by at least 0.5pp each month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline of at least 2% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in demand for goods and shelter, which depresses earnings across sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month -2% AND HOUST < previous month -2% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% mean) during periods of two consecutive months with both INDPRO and HOUST falling by more than 2%.
